title: Example 128 (B9, JBMC) read from equivalence --json
description: build.py now runs jvmcontract equivalence with --json and reads the library's Outcome instead of its console text (build-orchestration brief, step 1c). The verdict must agree with the exit code, and the result gains search (engine, checker, seconds, bounds, input range, shared callees, the own checker's path and solver numbers) and replay (where the witness was replayed: jvmcontract's bytecode interpreter), and a violation's counterexample gains found and shrinkRuns. The page now says the witness was replayed in jvmcontract's bytecode interpreter, not on the JVM. Example 128 is a JBMC violation on a record method related with --before-arguments, with a shrunk witness: its verdict, counterexample input/contract/actual, domain and proof line must be unchanged, with search.engine jbmc and replay.by interpreter added.
expected: example 128 gives its expected violation with the same witness as before: build.py prints 'as expected' and exits 0

resources.notes: a Crosscut B9 example: javac build and a JBMC proof that took 0.5 s
